User AnswerThe program covered essential topics such as flight planning,
meteorology, aircraft performance, airspace structure, regulatory and others.
The instructors demonstrated a high level of expertise and professionalism,
offering meaningful insights drawn from his wise industry experience, not less
in a OCC environment.

However, there were some areas where the course could be improved to better meet
operational needs, particularly for those who will have to work in a IOCC "GCC"
contexts such as Challenge.

Firstly, the structure of the course was occasionally "unclear", which made it
difficult at times to follow the logical progression of topics. Greater
organization and a clearer roadmap of the training content would enhance the
learning process. For those who attended previous aeronautical courses (Flight
dispatch / Pilot training or other) will have no problem to adapt quickly on
this, but as we are not all on the same level, i saw some of us lost in the
course, were some other they were well ahead. Additionally, the course lacked
sufficient examples directly related to the aircraft type operated by Challenge,
especially in the areas of performance calculations and operational limitations.
Unfortunately not helped as well from the training department of Challenge,
where they should have give us the access to the training manual and operational
manuals since the first day, as to do so, we could have covered some useful
information during FPL or NAV exercises. Including aircraft-specific case
studies would make the training more applicable and immediately relevant.

Another point for improvement involves route/ airspace study and airport
familiarization. There was limited focus on the actual network of destinations
served by Challenge, which is critical for dispatchers to gain situational
awareness and prepare for real-world scenarios. Moreover, more practical
exercises using the specific software tools used by Challenge would have
significantly enhanced the hands-on component of the course.

In conclusion, while the course provided a solid foundation in dispatch theory
and regulations, it would benefit from a more tailored and structured approach,
with greater emphasis on airline-specific procedures, software training, and
aircraft/route-specific examples.

I am confident that with these improvements, the course could offer even more
value to the next group.

That said, the instructor showed great potential and a strong grasp of the
subject matter. With access to more detailed information, regarding aircraft
performance and operational specifics (OMs, Charts and other) you could truly
extract 110% of his capabilities, delivering an even more impactful and
effective learning.

The program covered essential topics such as flight planning, meteorology, aircraft performance, airspace structure, regulatory and others.
The instructors demonstrated a high level of expertise and professionalism, offering meaningful insights drawn from his wise industry experience, not less in a OCC environment.

However, there were some areas where the course could be improved to better meet operational needs, particularly for those who will have to work in a IOCC "GCC" contexts such as Challenge.

Firstly, the structure of the course was occasionally "unclear", which made it difficult at times to follow the logical progression of topics. Greater organization and a clearer roadmap of the training content would enhance the learning process. For those who attended previous aeronautical courses (Flight dispatch / Pilot training or other) will have no problem to adapt quickly on this, but as we are not all on the same level, i saw some of us lost in the course, were some other they were well ahead. Additionally, the course lacked sufficient examples directly related to the aircraft type operated by Challenge, especially in the areas of performance calculations and operational limitations. Unfortunately not helped as well from the training department of Challenge, where they should have give us the access to the training manual and operational manuals since the first day, as to do so, we could have covered some useful information during FPL or NAV exercises. Including aircraft-specific case studies would make the training more applicable and immediately relevant.

Another point for improvement involves route/ airspace study and airport familiarization. There was limited focus on the actual network of destinations served by Challenge, which is critical for dispatchers to gain situational awareness and prepare for real-world scenarios. Moreover, more practical exercises using the specific software tools used by Challenge would have significantly enhanced the hands-on component of the course.

In conclusion, while the course provided a solid foundation in dispatch theory and regulations, it would benefit from a more tailored and structured approach, with greater emphasis on airline-specific procedures, software training, and aircraft/route-specific examples.

I am confident that with these improvements, the course could offer even more value to the next group.

That said, the instructor showed great potential and a strong grasp of the subject matter. With access to more detailed information, regarding aircraft performance and operational specifics (OMs, Charts and other) you could truly extract 110% of his capabilities, delivering an even more impactful and effective learning.
